subproblem.title: A boundaryless 1-current with integer densities on finitely many rays has constant integer multiplicities summing to zero (parent step 4)
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and C ∈ 𝒟_1(ℝ^P) with ∂C = 0 (C.boundary = 0). Let F be a finite set of unit vectors and g : ℝ^P → ℝ → ℝ such that, for every e ∈ F, g_e := g(e) is locally integrable on (0, ∞) and g_e(t) ∈ ℤ for almost every t > 0, and suppose C(ω) = Σ_{e∈F} ∫_{(0,∞)} g_e(t)·ω(te)(e) dt for every ω ∈ 𝒟¹(ℝ^P). Then there is m : ℝ^P → ℤ with Σ_{e∈F} m(e) = 0 and C(ω) = Σ_{e∈F} m(e)·∫_{(0,∞)} ω(te)(e) dt for every ω ∈ 𝒟¹(ℝ^P).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 1), C.boundary = 0 → ∀ F : Finset (Euclid P), (∀ e ∈ F, ‖e‖ = 1) → ∀ g : Euclid P → ℝ → ℝ, (∀ e ∈ F, LocallyIntegrableOn (g e) (Ioi 0)) → (∀ e ∈ F, ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume.restrict (Ioi (0 : ℝ))), ∃ k : ℤ, g e t = k) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 1, C ω = ∑ e ∈ F, ∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ), g e t * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 1) (t • e) (fun _ => e)) → ∃ m : Euclid P → ℤ, ∑ e ∈ F, m e = 0 ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 1, C ω = ∑ e ∈ F, (m e : ℝ) * ∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ), (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 1) (t • e) (fun _ => e)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 4 ("by the constancy theorem (Simon Ch. 6, 2.34, applied in coordinates in which ray(e_i) is an open half-axis ...), C⌞V_i = m_i[[ray(e_i)]]⌞V_i for some m_i ∈ ℤ" and "Testing ∂C = 0 with f ∈ C^∞_c(ℝ^P), f(0) = 1: 0 = C(df) = Σ_i m_i∫_0^∞ (d/dt)f(te_i) dt = −Σ_i m_i"); Simon 2.34 is chapter-06.txt lines 569–604. The "coordinates in which ray(e_i) is a half-axis" are realized by the parametrization t ↦ te_i and test functions that see only one ray. Uses sibling du_bois_reymond.
Notation: α[v] := α(fun _ => v) for a 1-covector α; C^∞ means ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞).
1. (Testing ∂C = 0.) Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support. The 0-form f̂(x) := f(x) (the constant alternating map of no arguments, ContinuousAlternatingMap.constOfIsEmpty) is a test 0-form on ℝ^P, and its exterior derivative satisfies (d f̂)(x)[v] = Df(x)v (extDeriv_constOfIsEmpty). Since ∂C = 0, 0 = (∂C)(f̂) = C(d f̂). By the hypothesis applied to the test 1-form d f̂ and the chain rule Df(te)e = (d/dt) f(te):
 (1.1) Σ_{e∈F} ∫_{(0,∞)} g_e(t)·(d/dt) f(te) dt = 0 for every C^∞ f with compact support.
2. (Test functions that see only one ray.) Fix e₀ ∈ F and a C^∞ function ψ : ℝ → ℝ with compact support and tsupport ψ ⊆ (0, ∞). Choose 0 < α ≤ β with ψ(s) ≠ 0 ⇒ α ≤ s ≤ β (tsupport ψ is a compact subset of (0, ∞)). Choose κ > 0 with κ < α²(1 − ⟨e, e₀⟩²) for every e ∈ F with ⟨e, e₀⟩² < 1 (finitely many positive bounds), and a C^∞ function χ : ℝ → ℝ with χ(0) = 1 and χ(s) = 0 for s ≥ κ (a smooth bump centred at 0 with radii κ/2 and κ). Put
 f(x) := ψ(⟨x, e₀⟩)·χ(|x|² − ⟨x, e₀⟩²).
 a. f is C^∞, being built from C^∞ maps by composition and multiplication.
 b. f has compact support: f(x) ≠ 0 forces α ≤ ⟨x, e₀⟩ ≤ β and |x|² − ⟨x, e₀⟩² < κ, hence |x|² < β² + κ.
 c. f(se₀) = ψ(s)·χ(0) = ψ(s) for every s ∈ ℝ, since ⟨se₀, e₀⟩ = s and |se₀|² = s².
 d. f(te) = 0 for every e ∈ F ∖ {e₀} and every t > 0. Put c := ⟨e, e₀⟩, so f(te) = ψ(tc)·χ(t²(1 − c²)). If ψ(tc) = 0 we are done. Otherwise tc ≥ α > 0, so c > 0; moreover c < 1, because c = 1 would give |e − e₀|² = 2 − 2c = 0, i.e. e = e₀. Hence c² < 1, t > tc ≥ α, and t²(1 − c²) ≥ α²(1 − c²) > κ, so the χ-factor vanishes.
3. (Each density is an integer constant.) Apply (1.1) to the f of step 2. For e ∈ F ∖ {e₀}, t ↦ f(te) vanishes on the open set (0, ∞), so its derivative vanishes there; for e = e₀, t ↦ f(te₀) = ψ(t). Hence ∫_{(0,∞)} g_{e₀}(t)·ψ'(t) dt = 0 for every such ψ. By du_bois_reymond (g_{e₀} is locally integrable on (0, ∞)) there is c₀ ∈ ℝ with g_{e₀} = c₀ almost everywhere on (0, ∞). Since also g_{e₀} is integer-valued a.e. on (0, ∞), and (0, ∞) has positive measure, there is t with g_{e₀}(t) = c₀ and g_{e₀}(t) = k ∈ ℤ; so g_{e₀} = k a.e. on (0, ∞). Define m(e₀) := k for e₀ ∈ F, and m(e) := 0 for e ∉ F.
4. (The formula.) For every ω, using g_e = m(e) a.e. on (0, ∞) (integrals of a.e.-equal functions agree) and pulling out the constant: C(ω) = Σ_{e∈F} ∫_{(0,∞)} g_e(t)·ω(te)[e] dt = Σ_{e∈F} m(e)·∫_{(0,∞)} ω(te)[e] dt.
5. (Σ m = 0.) Let b be a smooth bump on ℝ^P centred at 0 with inner radius 1 and outer radius 2 (C^∞, compact support, b = 1 on closedBall(0, 1), so b(0) = 1). Step 1 applies equally to the representation of step 4 (densities ≡ m(e)): 0 = Σ_{e∈F} m(e)·∫_{(0,∞)} (d/dt) b(te) dt. For a unit vector e, h(t) := b(te) is C^∞ with compact support (t ↦ te is a closed embedding), so h' is integrable on (0, ∞), h is continuous at 0 and h(t) → 0 as t → ∞; by the fundamental theorem of calculus on (0, ∞) (integral_Ioi_of_hasDerivAt_of_tendsto), ∫_{(0,∞)} h'(t) dt = 0 − h(0) = −1. Hence 0 = −Σ_{e∈F} m(e), i.e. Σ_{e∈F} m(e) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: ∂C = 0 tested on 0-forms f̂ gives Σ_e ∫_0^∞ g_e(t) (d/dt) f(te) dt = 0 for all smooth compactly supported f.
f(x) = ψ(⟨x, e₀⟩)χ(|x|² − ⟨x, e₀⟩²) equals ψ on ℝe₀ and vanishes on the other open rays of F.
Hence ∫ g_{e₀} ψ' = 0 for all ψ ∈ C^∞_c((0, ∞)); du_bois_reymond and integrality give g_{e₀} ≡ m(e₀) ∈ ℤ a.e.
Testing with a bump b, b(0) = 1, and ∫_0^∞ (d/dt) b(te) dt = −1 gives Σ_e m(e) = 0.

audit.reason: The constructed smooth tests isolate each ray. The declared constancy dependency and almost-everywhere integrality produce integer coefficients; testing a bump at the origin proves their sum is zero. All required support and integrability conditions are justified.
